evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2020-01-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2020-01-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/1 {"dueDate":"2020-05-05"} returned 200 with the new date. PATCH {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date was removed. PATCH on todo 3 changed its date to 2000-01-01 and then to 2099-01-01.
evidence.AC3: These POST dueDate values each returned HTTP 400: 2026-02-30, 01.02.2026, 2026-2-3, abc, 20260101, 2026-13-01, and the number 5. A PATCH with 2026-02-30 also returned 400. A datetime string in the JSON body hit a JSON syntax error because my shell quoting was bad, and that also gave 400, so it doesn't count as evidence.
evidence.AC4: With today = 2026-11-01 (UTC), GET /todos?overdue=true returned only todo 2 (2020-01-01, not done) and todo 5 (2026-10-31, not done). Todos left out: no due date, a future date, a due date of today, and a done todo with a past date (its overdue flag is false).
evidence.AC5: The page at / showed each todo's due date in its list item: 'past 2020-01-01', 'future 2099-01-01', 'today 2026-11-01', 'yest 2026-10-31', 'pastdone ✓ 2020-01-01'. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, only 'past 2020-01-01 überfällig' and 'yest 2026-10-31 überfällig' carried the word. The no-due, future, today and done-past todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only 'past' and 'yest', both marked überfällig.
